name: tag_config_fingerprint
hash: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical JSON text of `configuration`
definition: The Tag config fingerprint is the repo-defined Precondition token for the Tag CONFIG Mutations (D30 §2: tag_update, tag_delete, tag_move, tag_rename). It is computed over exactly what tag_get_config publishes for the target path, so the value a caller passes back as items[].expectedFingerprint is the value of the read it reasoned about. Ignition does not enforce it: a handler reads the target's configuration and compares the fingerprint itself.

readShape.note: tag_get_config emits the fingerprint of the configuration its own call returned, whatever `recursive` and `overridesOnly` it was given. The value a Mutation compares is the one from the default read of one exact target path (recursive=false, overridesOnly=false): a fingerprint taken from a recursive or overrides-only read covers a different subtree and fails that comparison with conflict.

canonicalJson.keys: object keys sort by Unicode code point
canonicalJson.whitespace: none; `,` between items and `:` between a key and its value
canonicalJson.strings: only `"`, `\` and the control characters below U+0020 are escaped, and a control character is always the six-character \u00xx form; every other character is raw UTF-8
canonicalJson.integers: exact decimal form, no exponent and no leading zeroes
canonicalJson.floats: the interpreter's shortest round-trip form (Jython 2.7 `repr` and Python 3 `repr` agree on every finite value a Tag configuration carries; subnormal doubles are the one known divergence and no vector uses one)
canonicalJson.null: the literal `null`; the D28 encoding converts a null to {"$ignition":"null"} before the fingerprint is taken, so a null key never appears in a captured configuration

over: the D28-encoded configuration, which is byte-for-byte the `configuration` value the read returns
coverage: The token covers the node(s) that read returned. It does not cover a Tag's children beyond that read (tag_update refuses a nested `tags` change for exactly this reason: a child is its own target with its own token), and a property Ignition does not report in the read is outside it.
raceWindow: D30 §2: the compare and the change are two steps, so a race window remains between the handler's read and system.tag.configure, in the same way D16 documents the final import race. No atomicity is claimed: a competing writer inside the window is not detected by the token, and the tag_update handler is the only thing that narrows it (Preflight reads every item before any item is dispatched, and MergeOverwrite cannot create a target that Preflight found missing).
notASecret: A fingerprint is derived from configuration data the same read publishes; it is a Precondition token, never a credential.

goldenVectors.name: explicit-null-property
goldenVectors.source: D28 rule vector; no non-recursive read of the ticket #6 Tag provider root carried an explicit null
goldenVectors.documentation: An explicit null property: the native read carries a real null, and D28 encodes it as the reserved-key object before the fingerprint is taken, so the encoding rule is part of the token.

goldenVectors.name: escaped-reserved-key-object
goldenVectors.source: D28 rule vector; the escape exists so a configuration value can carry the reserved key
goldenVectors.documentation: A configuration value carrying a literal $ignition key: D28 escapes the whole object and sorts its entries, and the canonical form sorts object keys as well, so both rules have to survive together.

goldenVectors.name: non-ascii-and-control-characters
goldenVectors.source: escape rule vector; non-ASCII text and a control character are the two cases where two implementations can silently disagree
goldenVectors.documentation: Non-ASCII text stays raw UTF-8 and a control character is always the six-character \u00xx form, which is what makes the Jython and the Python copy of this rule agree byte for byte.

goldenVectors.name: atomic-tag-as-recorded
goldenVectors.source: recorded from the phase4-live G4b run 35668653064 (workflow `Phase 4 Live Gateway G4b`), where the same read and the same fingerprint were observed on the 8.3.8 and the 8.3.9 row: the `tag_get_config` read of [default]IgnitionMCP_CI/WriteTarget
goldenVectors.documentation: A memory Int4 AtomicTag exactly as a live Gateway reports it. Note `path`: the Gateway answers a native BasicTagPath object, which the handler's normalization publishes in its own native-object form, so the fingerprint is taken over that form.

goldenVectors.name: synthesized-node-for-a-missing-path
goldenVectors.source: recorded from the phase4-live G4b run 35668653064 (workflow `Phase 4 Live Gateway G4b`), where the same read and the same fingerprint were observed on the 8.3.8 and the 8.3.9 row: the read of [default]IgnitionMCP_CI/Missing, a path that is not there
goldenVectors.documentation: A Gateway does not answer an empty list for a path that is not there: it answers this synthesized node, `tagType: Unknown`, with its own deterministic fingerprint. That is why a CONFIG Mutation's existence check is `system.tag.exists` and not this read, and why the check has to run before the fingerprint compare: a caller holding this token could otherwise merge-create the target.

encoding: The fingerprint is taken over the D28 `ignition-null-v1` encoding of the read, which is exactly the `configuration` value tag_get_config publishes: a null becomes {"$ignition":"null"} and an object carrying a literal $ignition key is escaped as {"$ignition":"object","entries":[[key, value], ...]} with its entries sorted.
